config.atom_rule: four digits, all numeric, not starting 00

criteria.detail: 20 consecutive months, 2021-01 through 2022-08, the span this code carries one good on every leg; CHINA 21.0%, JAPAN 28.3%, MEXICO 42.4%, each present in all 20 months, and the next destination is PHILIPPINES at 2.5%; the read-out's cell one wanted twelve months and two anchors, and this is twenty months and three
criteria.name: B35-TG-1

criteria.detail: the carrier as configured is a star, 4 vertices and 3 edges, so b1 = E - V + 1 = 0; there is no independent loop on it and therefore no H1 obstruction to read, whatever the prices do. A second origin on the same three destinations would give V=5, E=6, b1=2. This costs nothing and it is decisive, which is why it runs before the floor and the count
criteria.name: B35-TG-2

criteria.detail: a square needs two classes at each of two positions and this feed gives one buyer class per destination, so the square sum has no second term; the reading this carrier supports is dispersion across positions, and a scalar field with one potential per position accounts for that, which places it in the common-answer cell rather than the distinguishing one
criteria.name: B35-TG-3

criteria.detail: one good, one origin, three destinations, 20 months: the most expensive anchor is between 1.247 and 1.610 times the cheapest, mean 1.450, and the gap never closes; the ordering is stable, with CHINA dearest in 16 of 20, JAPAN dearest in 4 of 20, and MEXICO cheapest in 18, JAPAN cheapest in 2
criteria.name: B35-TG-4

criteria.detail: the floor is measured, not asserted: 18 of 116 destination months land within 1e-4 of a whole cent per pound against a uniform expectation of 0.02 per cent, so the grid is one cent a pound, $0.0220 a kg; the thinnest monthly gap between the dearest and cheapest anchor is $0.537 a kg, 24.3 times that floor, and the mean gap is 45.6 times it
criteria.name: B35-TG-5

criteria.detail: the two routes that would give this carrier a loop or a square are named with what each buys and where the data sits; neither is fetched here, and the arm stays shut on the counting gate rather than on any number
criteria.name: B35-TG-6

d22.meaning: b1 is the number of independent closed loops, and an obstruction of the H1 kind lives on a loop; a star has none, so no amount of price dispersion here can form one
d22.shape: star: one origin, one edge to each destination
d22.what_would_change_it: a second origin shipping the same good to the same three destinations gives V=5, E=6, b1=2

report.reading_available: H0 and dispersion: which class reaches which position and at what price, with the price difference between positions explainable by a potential on the positions

second_class_at_one_position.what_it_would_be: two buyer classes inside one destination paying different prices for the same code, which this feed cannot see because it stops at the border
second_class_at_one_position.where_it_would_come_from: the importing country's own customs or wholesale reporting, which is a different channel from this one

second_origin.what_it_buys: two independent loops, so a loop sum exists and the scalar-field prediction of exactly zero becomes readable on this carrier

reshape.why: gate two is what closes this arm, and it closes it on shape rather than on data quality: twenty clean months on a star still have b1 = 0
